instructions.resync_main: Another pull request merged into the base branch and this branch no longer merges cleanly. Run `git fetch origin && git merge origin/$base`. Resolve every conflict by keeping both sides' changes (never drop rows or code that came from $base). Rerun the targeted tests for the files you touched, confirm `git rev-list --count HEAD..origin/$base` prints 0, commit the merge, then finish the step again.
instructions.fix_and_resubmit: First merge the latest base branch into your branch (`git fetch origin && git merge origin/$base`). Then fix what is listed above, commit, and finish the step again. If a PR check failed, read its log first (`gh pr checks <pr>`, then `gh run view <run-id> --log-failed`). If the failing test is one this branch didn't touch: when it is listed in docs/tracking/FLAKY.md, rerun only the failed job once (`gh run rerun <run-id> --failed`); otherwise fix it in its own commit ('test: fix pre-existing failure in <test>') and say so in your summary.

sprint.cmd: git ls-remote --heads origin | sed -n 's#.*refs/heads/##p' | grep -E -- '-sb-[12]$' | sort -V | tail -n 1

hotfix.cmd: az pipelines runs list --pipeline-ids "$PROD_PIPELINE_ID" --branch master --result succeeded --top 1 --query '[0].sourceVersion' -o tsv

ask_user.when: You need a decision or information from a human. Ask one clear question, give your recommended answer, and point to the evidence (a log line, a file, a PR check). Ask whenever you'd otherwise be guessing; search the repo first for what you can find out yourself.

impossible.title: Impossible
impossible.when: The work cannot be done as asked.

plan_ready.title: Plan ready
plan_ready.when: The plan is complete and needs no decision from a human. Additive schema changes (new tables, columns or MCP tools) are routine: list them under a 'Schema changes' heading in the plan and take this transition.

scope_changed.title: Scope changed
scope_changed.when: A finding changes what the ticket can deliver. Give your recommended option and the alternative. If the ticket only bundles several tasks, plan the first and put the rest in proposed_tickets. Before asking whether something already exists, search the repo for it and state what you found.

plan_needs_approval.title: Plan needs approval
plan_needs_approval.when: Only when the plan reverses an accepted ADR, drops or rewrites existing data, adds an external service or spends money. Finish with the full plan in your result; your reason names the one decision and your recommendation.

needs_product_context.title: Needs product context
needs_product_context.when: You need product context the ticket and the repo's docs and ADRs don't give. Say what you'd assume otherwise.

ready_for_testing.title: Ready for testing
ready_for_testing.when: The work is complete and should go to testing.

checks.name: Merges cleanly with the base branch
checks.cmd: git fetch -q origin $base && git merge-tree --write-tree HEAD origin/$base > /dev/null

items: The change contains nothing conductor-specific (no workflow or agent configuration, no notes for conductor); everything committed is useful to the other developers on this repository.

pr_ready_for_review.title: PR ready for review
pr_ready_for_review.when: The work is done and you want Ben to review the PR before it goes further. Start your summary (the PR description) with what changed in at most three bullets, what to look at first, and anything you couldn't verify, such as the Windows leg. Take this only once every question you had is answered: the summary hands off finished work and asks nothing.
